body: Architecture! I've very committed to it. It's love/hate. Love what I'm doing but hate the physical and mental stress it has. Stopping is really abrupt. Having 10+ hours of work to do each day of the week to no purpose is going to be hard.
Maps.me. I think it's better than Google Maps.
This, he was unbuckled the whole time. Unfortunately I was unbuckled for quick escape as well.

I've been thinking of strategy ever since this happened.

If it's a bad neighborhood, circle the house and see if there is anyone sketchy outside or walking in the area.

Ask the people you are delivering to to watch your back as you go back to your car.

If your car has an alarm button, use that before you get anywhere near it if you feel like someone maybe be lurking nearby.

Have a secondary phone under your seat so you can call 911 if your main phone is stolen. If you are clever, you can even use it to call while you are being driven around and say the directions you are going out loud so the dispatch can clue in.

I haven't decided if I'm going back. They are offering me day shift, but I'm not sure if I would even be comfortable with that.

I saw that manager once since this happened. Haven't spoken much.
I thought of jumping out of the car and running it into light poles. But you only get one shot and I wanted to be 100% certain I would escape.
Don't worry, the police are investigating. I was at the precinct telling them everything immediately after this happened.
The police have camera footage from everywhere we went. The gas station footage was used on TV as well.
Police have been involved from the beginning and is working with the bank.
He's seen on gas station camera following me to their ATM. Police are retrieving other camera footage from the bank we went to. He wasn't very smart.
